raw_response:
I am old now, so I do not want to take big risks. On my 9 mu, I will still do what has kept the family steady: most of the land in wheat-maize rotation, and a smaller piece in cotton. Wheat and maize are the backbone here, and cotton gives another bit of cash if the price is alright. I only finished primary school, so I do not count too finely. I mostly follow what worked before, watch what the neighbors do, and keep one eye on cost because my family is small and some people are away working.

This year I will put about 6 mu into wheat-maize and 3 mu into cotton. For wheat, I will sow in early October like usual, using bought local improved seed, not anything too fancy. I will put enough fertilizer so the crop does not turn weak, but I will not push too hard because fertilizer and water both cost money. I will irrigate around three times if the weather is normal. After wheat harvest in June, I will hurry to plant summer maize on the same 6 mu right away, with simple tillage because the turnaround is tight. For cotton, I will keep only 3 mu because I am getting older and cotton takes more watching and picking. I will manage it a bit carefully, but not too heavily, because labor is tight and I cannot spend too much cash at once.
